description: Turns typed text into a rhythm by spelling it out in Morse code, one clock to a unit of time

params.text: Sets how many units of time a dot lasts, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of time a dash lasts, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of silence separate one letter from the next, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of silence separate one word from the next, 0 to 9

inputs.text: Steps the sequence on by one unit; every change from 0V to any other voltage counts as a clock
Any change from 0V to another voltage here takes the sequence back to its first unit; clocks arriving in the moment after that are ignored

outputs.text: 10V while the current unit is part of a dot or a dash and 0V while it is silence; it holds its value between clocks
A 1ms pulse of 10V each time the sequence returns to its first unit

notes: the module does nothing until there is both a clock and some text: click the large black screen and type, and click outside it to stop typing
only the letters A to Z and the digits 0 to 9 are understood; anything else is left out
the strip along the bottom shows how long the sequence has become
international Morse code is used, and the four knobs come up at the standard lengths: a dot of 1, a dash of 3, 3 between letters and 7 between words
one unit of time is the gap between two clocks, so a fast clock gives the most usable rhythms
menu: Use DD cable color scheme - Light — replaces Rack's cable colour list with five colours of the maker's, after a confirmation step; the item ends in Dark under the Rack dark-panel setting
